title: Batch job scheduler: queue order, blocked deps, team summary
scenario: Event-driven simulation of a day of batch jobs on 2 workers: priority queue (higher number first), dependencies, scripted failures with retries, blocked jobs (missing deps, cycles), and a per-team / lateness / utilization summary.

verified.why_correct: The regex makes both parts optional, which looks like it would accept an empty string, but `not any(match.groups())` rejects that. Bare digits are minutes (m4's '30'), and '1h' / '45m' / '1h30m' all parse to the right minute counts.

A DFS with open/done states; meeting an 'open' node means the path from that node to here is a cycle, so path[path.index(dep):] is exactly the cycle (c1, c2). Unknown deps are skipped here because missing_dep reports them. c3 depends on the cycle but is not on it, so it is not blocked; it ends up skipped.

bugs.title: Queue modified while iterating it
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_morning_wave: m3 runs 06:00-06:30 on w2 and m2 waits until 06:30-07:15, although m2 (priority 5) outranks m3 (priority 3) and two workers were free at 06:00.
bugs.why: queue.remove(state) inside the loop shifts the list, so the iterator skips the next element. At 06:00 m1 starts, m2 is skipped, and m3 takes w2. This only matters when two or more workers are free at once, which happens only at the start of the morning wave.
hints: Two workers are free at 06:00 and m2 outranks m3. Why does m3 start first?
Look at the loop that starts queued jobs. What happens to the list while it is being walked?
Iterate over a copy: for state in list(queue).
probes: Why doesn't the afternoon wave show the same problem?
How else could you write this loop so that removal is safe?

bugs.title: Release time missing from the queue tie-break
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_afternoon_wave: a2 starts at 13:42 on w2 and a3 at 14:00 on w1; it should be the other way round (a3 was released earlier, same priority).
bugs.why: a2 and a3 are both priority 4. a3 was released at 13:05 and a2 at 13:10, so a3 should go first, but without release in the key the id decides and a2 wins.
hints: At 13:42 one worker frees up. Which of a2 and a3 has waited longer?
Look at the key the queue is sorted by.
Put self.release between priority and job_id.
probes: Why does a6 still start at 14:12 either way?
The docstring said 'earlier release' all along. How would you test the key directly?

bugs.title: Only the first dependency is checked
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_blocked: b1 is missing from blocked ({b2, c1, c2} only), and its status is skipped rather than blocked.
bugs.why: The `return None` is inside the loop, so the function gives up after the first dependency. b1's first dep (m1) exists, so its missing second dep zz-missing is never seen; b1 is not blocked and just waits until it is skipped at the end of the day.
hints: b1 depends on m1 and zz-missing. Why isn't it blocked?
Step through missing_dep for b1. How many dependencies does it look at?
Dedent `return None` so it runs after the loop.
probes: Why does b1 end up 'skipped' instead of crashing the scheduler?
Why is b2 still reported correctly?

bugs.title: Event log shared between all jobs
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_event_log: m5's log holds every event of the day (starts on both workers, the afternoon wave) instead of its own 4 entries.
bugs.why: The default list is created once, when the function is defined. Every JobState built without events gets that same list, so each job's log holds the whole day's events.
hints: m5's log contains starts on both workers and events from 13:00. Whose events are those?
Where does each JobState's events list come from?
Default to None and create a new list per instance.
probes: Why does nothing else in the report change?
Why isn't events=list() as a default any better?

bugs.title: groupby over unsorted jobs
bugs.old:
ordered = sorted(states.values(), key=lambda s: s.job.team)
    for team, group in groupby(ordered, key=lambda s: s.job.team):
bugs.new: for team, group in groupby(states.values(), key=lambda s: s.job.team):
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_teams: etl shows jobs 2 / succeeded 0 / busy 0, ml/bi/ops show 1 job each with 0 busy; the real totals are bi 5/4/105, etl 6/4/205, ml 4/3/90, ops 3/0/10.
bugs.why: itertools.groupby only groups consecutive items. In file order the teams are interleaved, so each team comes up several times and summary[team] is overwritten by its last run (e.g. etl ends up as just c1 and c2).
hints: etl has 6 jobs in jobs.csv. Which 2 did the summary count?
What does groupby assume about its input order?
probes: How would you write this with a dict / defaultdict instead?
Why can't you call len() on the group directly?

bugs.title: Finishing exactly at the deadline counted as late
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_late: ["a6", "a9"] instead of ["a6"]; a9 ends exactly at its 14:00 deadline.
bugs.why: a9 ends at 14:00 with a 14:00 deadline. The README says that is on time; >= reports it as late.
hints: When does a9 finish, and what is its deadline?
Look at the comparison in late_jobs.
probes: Which other comparisons in the package are boundary-sensitive?
If deadlines had seconds, would anything change?

context_qa.a: It reads the worker count from config.json, loads jobs.csv and failures.csv, computes blocked jobs with dag.blocked_jobs, runs scheduler.simulate, and turns the JobStates into the jobs / events / blocked / summary sections.

context_qa.q: How does simulate move through time?
context_qa.a: `now` starts at the earliest release. Each step finishes running attempts with end <= now, adds newly ready jobs to `queue`, sorts it by Job.queue_key, starts queued jobs on free workers (lowest number first), then jumps to the next end time or future ready_at. When nothing is upcoming, any job still pending is marked skipped.
A tuple that sorts ascending: it starts with -priority so higher priorities come first, followed by the remaining tie-break fields.

context_qa.q: How are failures and retries handled?
context_qa.a: scheduler._finish checks whether the attempt number is in failures[job_id]. If it is, it logs fail@time and, when attempts <= max_retries, puts the job back to pending with ready_at = now + 10; otherwise the job is failed. Non-failing attempts log done@time and succeed.
The Job, an events list, status, attempts, ready_at, start/end/worker of the latest attempt, and busy (minutes across all attempts). log() appends to events.

context_qa.q: How does blocked_jobs pick a reason?
context_qa.a: For each job it asks missing_dep for an unknown dependency; if one is found the reason is missing_dep:<id>. Otherwise, if the job is in cycle_members(jobs), the reason is cycle.

context_qa.q: What shape is the team summary?
context_qa.a: team_summary returns {team: {jobs, succeeded, busy_min}}, built by grouping JobStates with itertools.groupby keyed on job.team.
